    <item>
      <title>US grants deportation reprieve to migrants from Ukraine and Sudan</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/us-migrants-deportation-ukraine-sudan</link>
      <description><p>DHS says migrants ‘retain protections’ after temporary protected status was set to expire on Monday</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/15/immigration-trump-midterms-reader-q-a">Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>More than 100,000 people from Ukraine and Sudan can stay in the United States without immediate risk of deportation, the Department of Homeland Security said, in what amounts to a temporary reprieve after their right to stay in the country was set to expire on Monday.</p><p>Temporary protected status was set to end on Monday for about 101,000 Ukrainians and 1,800 Sudanese. But the DHS said an announcement “will be made at the appropriate time”. Until then, the department said in a written statement, Ukrainians and Sudanese in the US covered by those temporary measures “retain protection”. The department did not indicate how long they could stay or when a final announcement would be made on their status.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/us-migrants-deportation-ukraine-sudan">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/kenya-starvation-cult-leader-guilty-murder-190-children</link>
      <description><p>Paul Mackenzie and his church set up sect that ordered followers to starve themselves and their children, say prosecutors</p><p>A Kenyan court has found the starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie and about 30 others guilty of murder over the deaths of ⁠190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult-related disasters in recent history.</p><p>Mackenzie was arrested in 2023 after police received a tipoff, and weeks later authorities began uncovering bodies in shallow graves in the Shakahola forest near the coast ⁠in south-eastern Kenya.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/kenya-starvation-cult-leader-guilty-murder-190-children">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/drone-attack-market-al-dibab-west-kordofan-sudan</link>
      <description><p>Witness says drone struck twice at transport hub in al-Dibab, in one of deadliest single attacks of war</p><p>A drone strike near a market in southern Sudan on Sunday evening killed 80 people, mostly commuters catching rides home.</p><p>Ahmed Wadi, a witness, said the attack in the town of al-Dibab in West Kordofan state left “50 bodies who I helped bury, one of them my own brother Mohamed”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/drone-attack-market-al-dibab-west-kordofan-sudan">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Ebola cases in Kenya highlight US failures amid Trump cuts to key services</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/ebola-cases-kenya-us-quarantine</link>
      <description><p>Opposition to US-led quarantine center in Kenya follows sweeping funding cuts and withdrawal from WHO</p><p>An eighth person in Kenya has tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in the country’s first-ever cluster of cases of the virus, as the second-largest outbreak in history has killed more than 4,300 and sickened more than 9,000 people in the region.</p><p>It highlights the diminished role the US has played in the worsening Ebola outbreak by building a controversial quarantine center in Kenya, pulling back health support globally, and banning travelers from certain countries. All of this has also reduced the ability to identify and respond to the outbreak and exacerbated mistrust.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/ebola-cases-kenya-us-quarantine">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Hilarious quips and ‘100,000-volt’ energy: the hypemen (and women) redefining Afrobeats music</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/18/lagos-hypemen-redefining-afrobeats-music-afrohype</link>
      <description><p>Style of emceeing based on high-octane, ad-libbed vocals has flourished thanks to its unique way of captivating crowds</p><p>For the 2015 freshmen cohort of the history degree programme at the University of Lagos, their classmate’s first-semester presentation was so captivating that they began calling him Toby Shang, after the 16th-century Chinese dynasty he had focused on.</p><p>His crowd engagement that day had been harnessed from his high school days as a ginger-man (energiser) in a three-man band and as a private tutor. By his final year at university, his viral catchphrases and infectious energy had resulted in a hit song, Shedibalabala. Today, he is one of the self-acclaimed “evangelists and pioneers” in the Afrobeats sub-genre some are now calling Afrohype or lamba.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/18/lagos-hypemen-redefining-afrobeats-music-afrohype">Continue reading...</a></description>

News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 03:02:22 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Europe</category><title>Live: Curfews come into effect around France to combat looting</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261020-live-curfews-come-into-effect-around-france-to-combat-looting</link><description>
Curfews came into effect in cities across France, including Paris, Bordeaux, Nice and Lyon, as French police attempted to crack down on looting during protests. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has said that implementing a state of emergency is not out of the question. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4ba3c65c-cc29-11f1-b901-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3RV38Z.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4ba3c65c-cc29-11f1-b901-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3RV38Z.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2b1c7b6a-cc31-11f1-b8dd-5384bc80ef02</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 02:51:36 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4ba3c65c-cc29-11f1-b901-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3RV38Z.jpg">© Olivier Chassignole, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Zelensky accuses US of delaying missile deliveries as tensions rise</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261020-zelensky-accuses-us-of-delaying-missile-deliveries-as-tensions-rise</link><description>
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused the US on Monday of holding up deliveries of Patriot interceptor missiles already paid for by European allies, as tensions with President Donald Trump’s administration deepened over military aid and intelligence sharing.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/35a106a0-cbdc-11f1-844f-d1d2c32ebb87/w:1024/p:16x9/bb914f42bdf0a8c35c60195688087ff485fa414d.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/35a106a0-cbdc-11f1-844f-d1d2c32ebb87/w:1024/p:16x9/bb914f42bdf0a8c35c60195688087ff485fa414d.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">89de3ff6-cc29-11f1-a926-d518a0f5c63b</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 01:56:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/35a106a0-cbdc-11f1-844f-d1d2c32ebb87/w:1024/p:16x9/bb914f42bdf0a8c35c60195688087ff485fa414d.jpg">© Oleskii Filippov, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Technology</category><title>Japan launches mission to explore Mars' moons and bring back samples</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/technology/20261020-japan-launches-mission-to-explore-mars-moons-and-bring-back-samples</link><description>
Japan launched a spacecraft on Tuesday on a five-year mission to explore Mars' mysterious moons, Phobos and Deimos, and bring back samples for the first time. The $578 million project aims to deliver dust, soil and rocks to Earth in 2031, potentially shedding light on how the moons formed and the origins of life.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/af16faf0-cb94-11f1-9e48-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/1329e57e1d2112e42b31f522a1d6229f84f9f886.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/af16faf0-cb94-11f1-9e48-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/1329e57e1d2112e42b31f522a1d6229f84f9f886.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b995441e-cc25-11f1-ab45-9101ade8235e</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 01:29:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/af16faf0-cb94-11f1-9e48-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/1329e57e1d2112e42b31f522a1d6229f84f9f886.jpg">© Yuichi Yamazaki, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Spain floods kill four as torrential rain inundates eastern regions</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261019-spain-floods-kill-four-as-torrential-rain-inundates-eastern-regions</link><description>
Torrential rain battered eastern Spain on Monday, killing at least four people in recent days as floodwaters swept away cars, submerged roads and stranded residents. Emergency crews carried out more than 400 rescues in Valencia, where rainfall reached 700 litres per square metre in 24 hours in some areas.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e9c067e8-b287-11f1-a41a-991cccd3bb73/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-17T090156Z-1967335667-RC2UKNAXSDKS-RTRMADP-3-EUROPE-WEATHER-SPAIN-FLOODS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e9c067e8-b287-11f1-a41a-991cccd3bb73/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-17T090156Z-1967335667-RC2UKNAXSDKS-RTRMADP-3-EUROPE-WEATHER-SPAIN-FLOODS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9cd79e50-cc05-11f1-b217-5541766e675c</guid><pubDate>Mon, 19 Oct 2026 21:39:49 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e9c067e8-b287-11f1-a41a-991cccd3bb73/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-17T090156Z-1967335667-RC2UKNAXSDKS-RTRMADP-3-EUROPE-WEATHER-SPAIN-FLOODS.jpg">© Eva Manez, Reuters,</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Business</category><title>France tells online marketplaces to crack down on resale of looted items</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/business/20261019-france-tells-online-marketplaces-to-crack-down-on-resale-of-looted-items</link><description>
As thousands of shop owners are reeling from the weekend violence and looting, listings of apparently stolen items have been popping up online.  The government asked major second-hand marketplaces such as Vinted, eBay and Amazon to crack down on suspicious adverts. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f2ac1af2-cc02-11f1-a7cb-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-88daf37e.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f2ac1af2-cc02-11f1-a7cb-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-88daf37e.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">71ab27f4-cc02-11f1-80a1-033df4545f1a</guid><pubDate>Mon, 19 Oct 2026 21:24:55 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Yuka ROYER</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

Images of protests, some violent, are multiplying across Europe. Italians have been called to a general strike on November 20, while similar actions are planned for November 11 in Spain and Portugal.]]></description><guid isPermaLink="true">https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/10/20/italy-spain-belgium-portugal-social-unrest-spreads-across-europe-amid-soaring-energy-prices-and-a-housing-crisis_6759435_4.html</guid><link>https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/10/20/italy-spain-belgium-portugal-social-unrest-spreads-across-europe-amid-soaring-energy-prices-and-a-housing-crisis_6759435_4.html</link><media:content width="644" height="322" url="https://img.lemde.fr/2026/10/17/85/0/1024/512/644/322/60/0/e69281a_ftp-1-m1zajatifpuw-afp-d3lk2m4-1024.jpg"><media:description type="plain">Protest against the housing shortage, soaring rents, and for higher wages, at Rossio Square in Lisbon, on October 17th, 2026.</media:description><media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">FILIPE AMORIM/AFP</media:credit></media:content></item><item><title><![CDATA[Brazil court gives Meta 24 hours to prove equal treatment of Lula and Bolsonaro]]></title><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 04:17:52 +0200</pubDate><description><![CDATA[Lula's campaign has alleged that the US tech giant is suppressing the incumbent president's online content. His party has filed complaints with the Organization of American States and the United Nations.]]></description><guid isPermaLink="true">https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/10/20/brazil-court-gives-meta-24-hours-to-prove-equal-treatment-of-lula-and-bolsonaro_6759369_4.html</guid><link>https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/10/20/brazil-court-gives-meta-24-hours-to-prove-equal-treatment-of-lula-and-bolsonaro_6759369_4.html</link><media:content width="644" height="322" url="https://img.lemde.fr/2026/10/19/516/0/6192/3096/644/322/60/0/59e8c00_ftp-1-w5hbvorclx1w-5389362-01-06.jpg"><media:description type="plain">Supporters of Brazil's President and presidential candidate Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva hold masks depicting Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg with red horns during a demonstration in front of Meta's headquarters in São Paulo, Brazil, on October 19, 2026.</media:description><media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">NELSON ALMEIDA / AFP</media:credit></media:content></item><item><title><![CDATA[The Saudi state's ambiguous stance on Osama bin Laden and Al-Qaeda]]></title><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 04:00:06 +0200</pubDate><description><![CDATA['On the Saudi Trail of 9/11' (3/4). In the early 1990s, the break between Riyadh and the leader of Al-Qaeda appeared complete. Osama bin Laden was forced into exile after fiercely opposing the American military presence in Saudi Arabia during the Gulf War. However, documents from the FBI and the CIA later revealed that certain religious circles within the kingdom never severed ties with the terrorist group.]]></description><guid isPermaLink="true">https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/10/20/the-saudi-state-s-ambiguous-stance-on-osama-bin-laden-and-al-qaeda_6759336_4.html</guid><link>https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/10/20/the-saudi-state-s-ambiguous-stance-on-osama-bin-laden-and-al-qaeda_6759336_4.html</link><media:content width="644" height="322" url="https://img.lemde.fr/2026/09/25/15/0/1347/673/644/322/60/0/4863ee0_upload-1-zbtsxtbzgxly-ap9909010770.jpg"><media:description type="plain">A poster depicting Al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden is sold in Rawalpindi, Pakistan, September 1999.</media:description><media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">B.K. BANGASH / AP</media:credit></media:content></item><item><title><![CDATA[Japan launches spacecraft on historic Mars moon mission]]></title><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 01:59:42 +0200</pubDate><description><![CDATA[The probe is set to land on Mars moon Phobos, where it will collect at least 10 grams of material during its mission. Scientists hope it will reveal how the planet Mars and its two moons formed.]]></description><guid isPermaLink="true">https://www.lemonde.fr/en/science/article/2026/10/20/japan-launches-spacecraft-on-historic-mars-moon-mission_6759270_10.html</guid><link>https://www.lemonde.fr/en/science/article/2026/10/20/japan-launches-spacecraft-on-historic-mars-moon-mission_6759270_10.html</link><media:content width="644" height="322" url="https://img.lemde.fr/2026/10/19/330/0/3968/1984/644/322/60/0/da0b148_ftp-1-v0cezlfr3zcr-2026-10-19t234952z-1172577292-rc2m6oaemdis-rtrmadp-3-japan-space-phobos.JPG"><media:description type="plain">The H3 rocket carrying the Martian Moons Exploration (MMX) rover bound for Mars' moon Phobos lifts off from the Tanegashima Space Center in Minamitane, Japan, October 20, 2026.</media:description><media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">KYODO / via REUTERS</media:credit></media:content></item><item><title><![CDATA[On tour in the Persian Gulf, Macron seeks a solution to soaring fuel prices]]></title><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 00:44:54 +0200</pubDate><description><![CDATA[The president began a three-day trip  to Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, and Qatar on Monday, hoping to 'secure' France's energy supplies. But the Gulf monarchies, whose hydrocarbon exports have plummeted due to the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, have little more leverage than Paris over the confrontation between the US and Iran.]]></description><guid isPermaLink="true">https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/10/20/on-tour-in-the-persian-gulf-macron-seeks-a-solution-to-soaring-fuel-prices_6759237_4.html</guid><link>https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/10/20/on-tour-in-the-persian-gulf-macron-seeks-a-solution-to-soaring-fuel-prices_6759237_4.html</link><media:content width="644" height="322" url="https://img.lemde.fr/2026/10/19/571/0/4189/2094/644/322/60/0/bb667a7_ftp-1-kqjrklz5xzg6-2026-10-19t092903z-164028296-rc286oaprspn-rtrmadp-3-gulf-france-kuwait.JPG"><media:description type="plain">French President Emmanuel Macron and the Emir of Kuwait, Sheikh Meshal Al Ahmad Al Jaber Al Sabah, attend a signing ceremony at Bayan Palace in Kuwait City, October 19, 2026.</media:description><media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">Benoit Tessier/REUTERS</media:credit></media:content></item></channel></rss>

      <description>While Hong Kong is betting on its established banking network to bring stablecoins into mainstream finance, Singapore is seeking to make regulated digital currencies easier to use.

      <description>China is ready to commercialise a 200-kilovolt transmission electron microscope with an information resolution down to 0.1 nanometres that could introduce a new challenger into a market long dominated by the US and Japan.
Developed by Hefei-based manufacturer CIQTEK, the microscope features a point resolution of 0.25nm and an information limit of 0.1nm – on par with leading workhorse models on the market.
This marks a shift for the country’s expanding advanced electron microscopy industry from...</description>

    <item>
      <author>Reuters</author>
      <dc:creator>Reuters</dc:creator>
      <description>Australian barber Ricky Jefferies has been hailed as a hero ⁠for running out of ⁠his store to detain a man who ⁠authorities allege deliberately drove a car into lawmaker Helen Haines in the small town of Wangaratta, an incident that has shocked the country.
Jefferies had just finished haircuts for a young family on Monday when he said he heard a “loud bang” outside his shop and realised the ‌driver of a Toyota LandCruiser had struck Haines, leaving her badly injured.
“It was crazy, I just ran...</description>

      <description>Thailand and Cambodia have agreed to dial down the rhetoric and use a hotline between their navy commanders to avoid flashpoints over a vast contested patch of energy-rich seas in the Gulf of Thailand, according to a UN-backed mediation panel at The Hague tasked with helping to settle the dispute between the neighbours.
The Southeast Asian countries have also squabbled for decades over the demarcation of their 800km (500-mile) land border, where clashes last year killed scores on both sides and...</description>

      <author>Zoey Zhang</author>
      <dc:creator>Zoey Zhang</dc:creator>
      <description>A Chinese AI girl group has sparked intense online backlash after announcing that one of its virtual members was “pregnant” to explain her departure.
BABYQUEEN, a four-member, K-pop-style AI girl group managed in Liaoning province in northeastern China, formed in September and has around 1,100 followers.
On October 13, the group posted an announcement written from member Mity’s perspective. Saying she was “pregnant” and would pause all public activities, Mity asked fans to respect her privacy...</description>

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Mon, 19 Oct 2026 22:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ New 'Blade Runner 2099' trailer is a space fan's dream with sinister starships and strange exoplanets (video) ]]> Cue the depressing rain, dark trench coats, and a dire dystopian dirge because the Blade Runner 2099 trailer is here!

Cyberpunk is charging back in confident fashion with Prime Video's latest detour into the neon-drenched dystopia of humans and rogue replicants first introduced in director Sir Ridley Scott's "Blade Runner" from 1982, then revisited in Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049."

Arriving Nov. 25, 2026, "Blade Runner 2099"'s plot turns the tables as resentful artificial beings are now the ones running the show and hunting down Earth’s humans after a successful uprising against their original makers.

This newest atmospheric trailer was unveiled at last week’s New York Comic-Con and has us totally jacked to re-immerse ourselves in that noirish futuristic realm.

Check it out below:

It’s executive produced by showrunner Silka Louisa ("Shining Girls”) and stars Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh ("Everything Everywhere All at Once") as Olwen, playing a fading replicant Blade Runner who joins forces with Hunter Schafer’s ("Euphoria") Cora, a pure human on the run attempting to evade a squad of exterminating Blade Runners while examining their existential natures.

But aside from the dazzling visuals of the City of Angels at the gates of the 22nd century, fans will also be strapping in for some cool outer space action, as evidenced by fresh footage delivering some arresting scenes of space travel, off-world planets, and Yeoh in a bizarre helmet.

"Blade Runner 2099"'s cast includes Dimitri Abold ("The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes") and Lewis Gribben ("Somewhere Boy”) alongside Katelyn Rose Downey ("The Nun II"), Daniel Rigby ('Renegade Nell"), Johnny Harris ("A Gentleman in Moscow"), Amy Lennox ("Only Child"), Sheila Atim ("The Woman King") and Matthew Needham ("House of the Dragon”).

Launching with an 8-episode debut season and executive produced by Scott Free Productions, "Blade Runner 2099" and its new world order lands on Prime Video on Nov. 25, 2026.

]]> <![CDATA[ The X-Files Lego set is a wonderful bit of 90s sci-fi nostalgia ]]> Millennials get a lot of flak for being overly nostalgic, but I don't think that's fair. When the modern-day world has nothing to offer us but AI slop, shrinkflation and a sad acceptance that we can't be bothered to do anything about global warming. It's easy to see why we yearn for the days of Pogs, the Backstreet Boys, and Saved by the Bell.

One area that we definitely had it good in the 90s was sci-fi, when legendary shows like Star Trek: The Next Generation, Stargate SG-1, and — of course — The X-Files ruled our TV screens long before the age of streaming services. You can relive those glory days of alien conspiracies, spooky happenings and cell phones the size of a brick with the Lego Ideas The X-Files set.

This 1478 piece set is essentially two dioramas crammed into a single display piece. The top of the model depicts a spinning UFO floating above one of those iconic coniferous forests that dominated 90s sci-fi. Why? Because — thanks to some generous tax credits — it was cheaper to shoot in Vancouver, so that's where they all flocked.

Disney Plus / Hulu bundle: was $12.99 now $11.99
Catch Mulder and Scully in every season of The X-Files on Hulu, which is available bundled with Disney+ for only $11.99/month for the first six months, then increasing to $12.99/month.View Deal

Beneath the woodland scene, though, is the real star of the show: Mulder's office, squirrelled away in the basement of the FBI's J. Edgar Hoover Building in Washington, D.C. This dingy little office is where Scully meets "Spooky Mulder", kicking off a glorious sci-fi odyssey that would last for eleven seasons (and two movies).

Mulder's dingy little base of operations has been stunningly recreated here, with both overt references and subtle nods that X-Files fans will appreciate. The iconic "I want to believe" poster adorns the wall, alongside photographs of crop circles and a newspaper clipping from a paper called "The Lone Brickman" — a nice nod to "The Lone Gunmen". There's even an actual X-File sitting on the desk, and a cute Lego spoof of the "Face on Mars", with a photo on the wall that shows a Lego head on the moon.

The X-Files Complete Boxset: $160
Prefer to actually own your media? Make your way through this X-Files Complete Boxset on DVD. Just bear in mind that you will need a region-free DVD player to watch it with.

It's been a hot minute since I watched The X-Files (that DVD box set beside my TV is calling to me), but even so, I had a blast building my way down memory lane, remembering episodes as I assembled the diorama. I love the little touches, like the display cabinets filled with artifacts, the VHS tapes scattered around the office and the black oil spillage on the floor.

As with most Lego sets, the minifigures are half the joy. You get Mulder and Scully, obviously, with the dynamic duo of FBI agents both rocking flashlights (no smartphones with built-in lights back in the 90s). Mulder is wearing dark blue, while Scully is rocking an orangey brown suit, with both of them sporting an FBI badge.

Outside of the principal pair, you also get Skinner, Mr X, and the Cigarette Smoking Man. Mulder's partner-turned-nemesis Alex Krycek also gets a suitably devious-looking minifig. It's the gloves, they just make him look like a bad man (which, to be fair, he is). Finally, to ramp up the paranormal scale, we also get a pair of monster minifigs: a grey alien and Flukeman minifigures. The grey alien was a must-have, especially given the UFO floating atop this display piece, but the one-off monster of the week, Flukeman, felt like a weird choice.

Also, this John Doggett erasure will not stand. Sure, he could never replace Mulder, but Robert Patrick's seasons eight and nine run was excellent and he deserved a spot here.

And while I'm voicing minor gripes, the usual Lego FOMO tricks were in force with this set; if you pre-ordered, you got an exclusive gift set — Scully's Lab — free of charge. This extra little diorama isn't necessary, but it does feel like the collection is incomplete without it and it's not for sale separately, so you'll have to try your luck with eBay scalpers if you want it.

Speaking of Scully, Gillian Anderson has stated that after season 11 wrapped in 2018, she was done with the role. That wasn't entirely accurate, though, as she donned the lab gloves one more time for the Lego X-Files set advert. It's a short bit of fan service, but a nice touch, and, once again, it sparks those 90s neurons.

All these delicious Member Berries come at a price, though, and that's the price. This blast from the past will set you back $199 (£179 in the UK). That's no small chunk of change. But then again, anyone who wants this set is in their thirties or forties and can probably afford that outlay for the nostalgia trip. And look at it this way: when The X-Files debuted back in 1993, the price would only have been about $86.

I had a great time building the Lego X-Files set and if you're a fan of the series, you will too. Nostalgia often feels like a cheat code to our hearts, but there's nothing wrong with that. We deserve to remember the good times and the truth is that The X-Files was about as good as it ever got for sci-fi fans.

You can buy the Lego X-Files set now, available for $199/£179 from the Lego store.

]]> <![CDATA[ Japan launches historic MMX sample-return mission to Mars' moon Phobos (video) ]]>

Japan's groundbreaking mission to Mars is officially underway, headed to the Red Planet's mysterious moons Phobos and Deimos for a historic sample-return attempt.

The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launched today (Oct. 19) from Tanegashima Space Center in Japan, riding an H3 rocket that lifted off from Pad-2 at Tanegashima's Yoshinobu Launch Complex at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. local time in Japan on Oct. 20).

The JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency)-led MMX mission is bound for Mars orbit, where it will study the planet's two moons, Phobos and Deimos. If everything goes according to plan, MMX will become the first spacecraft to land on and return samples from Phobos for study back on Earth, which scientists think could shed light on a decades-old mystery about the moons' origins and reveal clues about the formation of the early solar system.

It was the 10th liftoff of Japan's expendable, two-stage H3 rocket, which was jointly developed by JAXA and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. After clearing its launch pad today, the 207-foot-tall (63 meters) launch vehicle flew a nominal trajectory through its ascent corridor over the Pacific Ocean, jettisoning its four solid boosters in pairs just before the flight clock reached two minutes. The rocket shed its payload fairings about one minute and 20 seconds later, exposing MMX to the vacuum of space for the first time.

H3's first stage, powered by two LE-9 rocket engines, channels a mixture of liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen to produce a combined thrust of 331,000 pounds (1,471 kN), according to Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. As the mission clock approached T+5 minutes, H3 executed its main engine cutoff procedure and separated from the second stage, which ignited its engines for a 5.5-minute burn about 10 seconds later.

All continued to go to plan after that. The H3's upper stage ignited its engine for a second time for a trans-Mars injection burn about one hour and four minutes after liftoff, a maneuver that lasted roughly six minutes and 25 seconds and took MMX to a maximum velocity of about 24,145 mph (38,858 kph).

MMX was released from the rocket's upper stage right on schedule, about one minute after the completion of that burn and roughly 71 minutes after liftoff. The success elicited loud cheers in mission control, which viewers saw and heard on JAXA's launch webcast.

MMX is now under its own power, and on course for Mars. The interplanetary transit will last about 10 months, with the spacecraft scheduled to arrive at the Red Planet in August 2027. When it does, MMX's propulsion module will execute an orbital insertion burn to place itself in a quasi-satellite orbit (QSO) around Phobos, which places MMX within the space around the moon as both circle Mars.

MMX will spend about three years in the Martian system, devoting much of that time to studying the 14-mile-wide (22 km) Phobos with its science instruments. ]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Oct. 19, 2016: Europe's ExoMars orbiter and Schiaparelli lander arrive at Mars ]]>

On Oct. 19, 2016, the European Space Agency's ExoMars mission arrived at Mars!

ExoMars 2016 consists of the Trace Gas Orbiter and the Schiaparelli lander. The orbiter and lander traveled there together and separated on Oct. 16, three days before the orbiter entered orbit around Mars, and the lander touched down on the planet's surface. But something went wrong during the lander's descent, and it crashed into the ground.

Schiaparelli did not survive the accident, but the Trace Gas Orbiter is still functional. It is currently circling the planet, looking for methane and other gases in the Martian atmosphere that could be evidence for possible biological activity.

Why it mattered

ExoMars 2016 was a landmark mission for the European Space Agency and designed to be the vanguard of a two-flight ExoMars program to send an orbiter, lander and rover to Mars.

Launched in March 2016, ExoMars 2016 aimed to achieve two goals for ESA and Russia. First, the mission aimed to use the Schiaparelli lander to test landing techniques that would be vital on a planned ExoMars 2018 rover. Second, the mission would deliver a critical orbiter around Mars to study the planet's atmosphere and serve as a communications link for that future Mars rover.

In the end, ExoMars 2016 was just a partial success, with ESA officials calling it "96% successful." due to the loss of the lander.

While Schiaparelli separated smoothly from the ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter spacecraft, it stopped communicating with Earth just 1 minute before its planned landing on Oct. 19. Photos from NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter at Mars later revealed what appeared to be its crash site and, nearby, its jettisoned parachute. Officials suspect Schiaparelli did not fire its descent thrusters as designed in order to slow itself enough for a safe landing. A data glitch was cited as its cause.

The Trace Gas Orbiter, meanwhile, continues to study Mars to this day and has spent 10 years and counting studying the Martian atmosphere.

The launch of ExoMars 2018, which includes the Mars rover Rosalind Franklin, was delayed by the Schiaparelli failure, as well as the loss of its Russian Proton rocket when ESA severed its partnership with Russia over that country's war on Ukraine.

The ExoMars rover is now expected to launch no earlier than 2028, with a landing on Mars expected in 2030.

In 2026, another country took aim at Mars on this day.

The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency attempted to launch the ambitious Martian Moons eXploration mission (called MMX) to land a probe on the Mars moon Phobos and return samples to Earth.

Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.

]]> <![CDATA[ The moon is shrinking. 10,000 cracks on the lunar surface reveal by how much ]]> The moon is shrinking, and scientists are narrowing in on exactly how much our natural satellite has dwindled over the years.

The moon is thought to have formed from a violent collision between a massive object and our young Earth roughly 4.5 billion years ago, and its interior is still gradually cooling off from this ancient collision. As it cools, the moon contracts, leading to a long, slow shrinking process. Now, in a new study, scientists think that they have figured out how much smaller the moon is actually getting.

In this new study, scientists analyzing images snapped by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) have spotted over 10,000 young faults, or cracks across the moon's surface. This helped them to figure out how much the moon has contracted over time, and they now estimate that the moon's radius has decreased by about 148 feet (45 meters) over the past 400 to 800 million years.

"The number of these young faults revealed in LROC images is much greater than I ever imagined," study lead Thomas Watters, a geologist and scientist emeritus at the Center for Earth and Planetary Studies at the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum, said in a statement. "As the interior of the moon continues to cool and contract, it is expected that the growth of existing faults and formation of new faults continues today."

With these LROC observations, researchers in this study saw a variety of different types of cracks and landforms across the lunar surface. This included lobate scarps, or long, curved structures that form when the moon's surface contracts, cracks and is pushed upwards; and small mare ridges, or narrow "wrinkles" in the lunar surface, across the dark plains on the moon.

Tectonic activity on the moon looks a lot different than it does on Earth. On our own planet, there are about 15 major tectonic plates. On the moon, there are no tectonic plates at all. Instead, the moon has a single-plate body meaning its outer shell is a single piece only broken by faults or other such cracks created by the moon contracting. This means that instead of faults or cracks appearing at tectonic plate boundaries, they are instead scattered all over the moon.

By mapping these thousands of different features, all created from the moon cooling and contracting over time, the researchers are piecing together lunar history. In addition to finding the extent to which the moon has shrunk over time, they also found that some areas of the moon are covered in many more faults than other areas, and the areas with fewer cracks and faults have thicker moon crust.

This led them to conclude that not only are these areas with thicker crust more stable, but they suggest that a great deal of the widespread cracks in the lunar surface were created later in the moon's history as, in its earlier years, its thick crust would have insulated the moon's warm interior and prevented cooling, contracting and cracking.

This work was described in a study published Oct. 14 in The Planetary Science Journal.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'They're kind of goth': NASA spacecraft gives mysterious brown dwarfs a close-up ]]> Using NASA’s SPHEREx spacecraft, astronomers have studied a host of "failed stars," also known as brown dwarfs.

These strange cosmic bodies straddle the line between planets and stars, possessing a mass between 13 and 80 times that of Jupiter (0.013 to 0.08 times the mass of the sun). They get the nickname failed stars because they form like stars from collapsing clouds of gas and dust but fail to gather enough mass to trigger the fusion of hydrogen to helium in their cores, the process that powers actual stars.

This formation process also means that brown dwarfs are cosmic loners, wandering the darkness of space alone, bereft of the light of a parent star. That description might sound like lyrics from a Type O Negative song ("Black No. 1," anybody?). And that's apt, according to the leader of the new study, which reveals that, chemically speaking, the atmospheres of these dark and cloudy worlds are not unlike those of our solar system's gas giant planets.

"They’re kind of goth," Zafar Rustamkulov, of the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), said in a statement. "Unlike exoplanets, free-floating brown dwarfs are completely independent celestial objects that will fade into eternity alone. We’re still learning how complex they are."

Rustamkulov added that, from Earth orbit, SPHEREx — short for Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer — sees wavelengths of light that are nigh-impossible to see with telescopes on the ground because water in Earth’s atmosphere absorbs them. That is important for bringing brown dwarfs into the light.

"We are picking up light from the deep, red clouds of brown dwarfs all over the sky," he said.

A forest (of brown dwarfs)

Brown dwarfs have been somewhat mysterious since their discovery in the 1990s, due to the fact that the small amount of nuclear fusion that occurs within them causes them to emit no more than a faint glow. That means that our understanding of their makeup, their storms, and their evolution really only comes from theory.

To help lift this observational darkness, the team turned to data from SPHEREx. They studied 37 nearby brown dwarfs in a spectrum of light including 102 wavelengths, from the deepest red our eyes can see to the invisible infrared light. These local failed stars spanned the full temperature range for brown dwarfs — from 4,000 degrees Fahrenheit to minus 10 degrees Fahrenheit (2,200 to minus 20 degrees Celsius).

Considering that the temperature of the sun is about 10,000 degrees Fahrenheit (5,500 degrees Celsius), you could definitely say brown dwarfs run cold.

The spectra of brown dwarfs seen by SPHEREx allowed the team to determine that their atmospheres are chemically rich in water, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and methane.

"We’re seeing the signatures of these molecules and how they change from object to object across the entire temperature regime," said team member J. Davy Kirkpatrick, also of Caltech. "Our paper concentrated on just three dozen, but we have thousands more that we are in the process of analyzing.

"I really want to see what bounds the universe places on the variety of brown dwarfs."

All my colors

Brown dwarfs have been routinely observed by other telescopes, including NASA's James Webb Space Telescope and the agency's now-retired Spitzer Space Telescope, but the wide wavelength coverage of SPHEREx has made it particularly useful in observing these failed stars. That's good news for astronomers waiting for change in the atmospheres of brown dwarfs as they age and grow cold.

The researchers found that some brown dwarfs observed by SPHEREx are at a stage of extreme change in which their clouds are clearing, creating atmospheres rich in methane.

The team may have discovered significant new details about brown dwarfs, but they are still on the proverbial mystery street when it comes to these strange celestial objects,

"The state-of-the-art models are capturing the general chemical trend, but when it comes to these cloudy transitions, the models are struggling to match the data," said Rustamkulov. "No two brown dwarfs are alike. Even at the same temperature, their spectra look quite distinct."

"This journey has turned many of us into accidental meteorologists. We know how hard it is to predict weather on our own planet, and we realize it's going to be just as challenging to explain the phenomena we see in these bizarre, cold objects," Kirkpatrick said. "The findings are a call to action to explore even more of these dark worlds."

As astronomers resond to that call to action, I will ponder how I could have worked Bauhaus' Goth classic "Bela Lugosi is Dead" into this article.

The team's research was published on Sept. 28 in The Astrophysical Journal.

]]> <![CDATA[ Elephant Island is an icy sight from orbit | Space photo of the day for Oct. 19, 2026 ]]>

Antarctica is a magnificent sight, and that beauty is visible all the way from space.

What is it?

Orbiting planet Earth, the European Space Agency's (ESA) Copernicus Sentinel-3 mission captured a close-up of West Antarctica.

Winter is ending in the Southern Hemisphere, meaning this is the peak of icy weather and sea ice in the Arctic.

In this image snapped by Sentinel-3, you can see a massive swath of ice which includes Elephant Island on the left-hand side. An ice-covered island off the Antarctic coast, Elephant Island floats in the Southern Ocean. It got its name both from the island's shape, which some liken to that of an elephant's head, and the fact that the island is home to a community of elephant seals.

Why is it incredible?

While a seal-inhabited island on the left floats near the Antarctic coast, across the water is a vast, frozen landscape. In just this snapshot, you can see about between 746 and 1,056 miles (1,200 to 1,700 kilometers) of the icy continent.

]]> <![CDATA[ Did a giant object collide with Earth to form the moon? ]]> For as long as humans have watched the night sky, we have wondered about the moon, pondering everything from its alien appearance to its influence over phenomena on Earth such as ocean tides, climate stability, and even the natural rhythms of many organisms.

Among the many questions we have about Earth's lone natural satellite, one remains preeminent: what are the moon's origins, and how long has it orbited Earth?

Today, the leading theory among astronomers is that deep in our planet's past — perhaps within roughly the first 100 million years of solar system history — Earth collided with a planet-sized object, creating the moon within a period that may have been as short as just a few hours. Known as the giant-impact hypothesis, this proposed event involves a hypothetical Mars-sized protoplanet astronomers call Theia. The material ejected into orbit by the powerful impact in question would have accumulated afterward, forming the moon that we observe today.

What do we know?

Birth of a lunar origin hypothesis

The evolution of this striking solution to one of the moon's most enduring mysteries goes back to 1946, when geologist Reginald Aldworth Daly was among the first to suggest that an impact event might explain the formation of the moon.

Before Daly, scientists had been leaning toward theories that involved Earth's rapid spin billions of years ago, when each day may have at one time lasted as little as 2 or 3 hours. Decades later in the 1970s, researchers William Hartmann and Donald Davis developed their own models involving collisions of large bodies left over from planetary formation, which could collide with younger planets.

Building on such ideas, other researchers went on to propose similar scenarios between the early Earth and a Mars-sized object. Early in the following decade, the concept eventually claimed its place as the leading lunar-formation process during a landmark conference held in Kona, Hawaii, in 1984.

Evidence of a planetary-scale collision

The popularity of the giant-impact hypothesis can be attributed to the multiple lines of evidence supporting the impact scenario. For instance, researchers have long recognized the similar stable-isotope ratios between both moon rocks and those from Earth, strongly suggesting a link between their origins.

Additionally, the unusually high angular momentum (or spin) of the Earth-moon system, when compared to observations of other rocky planets, also could be explained as one of the effects of a massive collision.

Further clues can be found in the moon's composition, which reveals a relatively small iron core and lower density. This is significant to astronomers, since a hypothetical giant impact would have seen the suspected Theia protoplanet's metallic core merging with the young Earth's interior — meanwhile, lighter mantle and crust material from both worlds would have become dislodged and blasted into orbit, eventually helping form the moon.

Another important piece of evidence involves the relative depletion of volatile substances (a chemical that easily turns into gas or vapor at room temperatures) in lunar material, which again suggests that it might have been lost during an extremely energetic event, an idea further supported by evidence that the early moon once possessed a substantial magma ocean.

What remains unknown?

New research expands on the Theia hypothesis

Still, several significant questions remain, including what precise conditions led to the impact, and how the resulting planetary material evolved into the moon as it appears today.

Recently, a new study by Adeene Denton of Southwest Research Institute and colleagues at the University of Arizona's Lunar and Planetary Laboratory put a new spin on the Theia hypothesis, suggesting that the suspected ancient impact may have been significantly influenced by the heat and physical strength of the two colliding bodies.

The team's findings challenge some long-held views about the giant-impact hypothesis, while lending new support to others. For instance, the team's simulations revealed that while some impacts lead to the creation of a disk of debris that later coalesces into a moon, under other conditions, simulations support the idea that the moon could have been formed in a remarkably short period of time — perhaps within around five hours.

However, one of the primary issues with determining the exact conditions of the giant-impact hypothesis involves the ongoing debate over the moon's age.

"There is a large controversy regarding the age of the moon," said Dr. Erik Asphaug, a planetary science professor at the University of Arizona's Lunar and Planetary Laboratory and one of the new study's co-authors.

In an email to Space, Asphaug explained some of the issues arising from this, since current estimates place the timing of the moon's formation anywhere from around 40 to 120 million years after the formation of the solar system. Therein lies part of the issue, according to Asphaug, who says this timing could have significant implications for models of the Theia impact.

If it had been an earlier collision, Asphaug says this would have involved a hotter Theia due to the greater degree of radiogenic heating; by contrast, a later impact would have meant a cooler and stronger Theia.

"I don't think we know enough yet to say the moon (and by corollary, the Earth) formed this way or that way," Asphaug told Space. "But knowing how temperature affects the result opens up a new dimension for viewing the problem, and that is always helpful because it shifts our frame of reference, like getting out of the car to have a walk around."

A lunar enigma in time and space

For researchers like Asphaug, understanding the moon's formation requires looking at it as more than just an event in space, but also as one in time. Doing so allows comparisons between three different metrics: isotopic decay, temperature-dependent material strength, and the geological record of debris striking other planets — a process through which he believes tighter constraints could be placed on precisely when the moon-forming impact might have occurred.

Adeene Denton, the study's lead author, also emphasized the introduction of the time component her team's research brings to the table, telling Space in an email that the outcome of the moon-forming impact could have depended significantly on the timing of the collision.

"Before, scientists have generally assumed that the outcome of the collision will be the same regardless of when it takes place," Denton wrote. "But now we know that temperature's effect on material properties, which is dictated by how old and/or cold the proto-Earth and Theia might be, alters things substantially."

By connecting impact simulations to data related to the moon's geochemical record, as well as models of early solar system formation, Denton thinks her team's work could help scientists better constrain precisely how and when the moon formed.

The mystery continues

For now, in terms of which possible scenario — an earlier or later collision event — emerges as being the most likely, Denton says it's still difficult to say.

"It depends on which scenarios for solar system formation you favor," Denton told Space.

"I am generally in favor of an earlier formation of the moon, consistent with a rapid planet-building phase in our solar system," Denton said, "but we can't neglect the possibility that the moon formed late."

While much work remains to be done, Denton and Asphaug believe their findings help significantly advance present efforts to resolve some of the questions about the giant-impact hypothesis — a few of which have lingered now for many years.

For Asphaug, however, such lingering questions may simply be part of the scientific process.

"Science has a way of wandering around for a long time until finally it all comes to focus," Asphaug said.

"I believe that will happen, in part thanks to this work, in the coming decade."

]]> <![CDATA[ Watch Japan launch a bold sample-return mission to Mars moon Phobos today ]]> Editor's note: Japan launched its bold MMX sample-return mission to the Mars moon Phobos on Oct. 19) at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT).
Watch a replay of the liftoff and read our launch story here.

Japan will launch an epic mission to Mars today (Oct. 19), and you can watch the action live.

The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is scheduled to lift off atop an H3 rocket from Japan's Tanegashima Space Center today at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. on Oct. 20 local Japan time).

You can watch it live via the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). Coverage will begin at 2:45 p.m. EDT (1845 GMT).

As its full name suggests, MMX will focus on Mars' two moons, Phobos and Deimos. They're both tiny compared to Earth's own moon; Phobos is just 14 miles (22 kilometers) wide, and Deimos is even smaller, with a diameter of about 8 miles (13 km).

They're also quite mysterious. While astronomers have a pretty clear understanding of our own moon's birth — it coalesced from material blasted into space when a Mars-sized planet slammed into Earth long ago — there's no consensus about Phobos and Deimos' origin story.

The duo "may be the remains of a massive impact on Mars that sent material into orbit around the planet, or they could be ancient asteroids that were captured by Mars' gravity billions of years ago," Tom Statler, MMX program executive and program scientist at NASA Headquarters, said in an Oct. 15 statement. (NASA is a partner on the mission, providing a scientific instrument, a technology demonstration, communication support and funding for American scientists on the MMX team.)

"Having the answer will help illuminate that early era when Earth and the other inner planets may have been acquiring much of their water and organic compounds," Statler added.

MMX will help provide that answer, if all goes according to plan.

The spacecraft will arrive in the Mars system in August 2027, then slip into orbit around Phobos a month later. It will study that moon and Deimos from a distance for about 18 months, then deploy the French-German Idefix rover onto Phobos' surface in early 2029.

The 55-pound (25 kilograms) Idefix "has two main tasks: providing information to prepare for the landing of the main spacecraft to collect samples, and analyzing the composition and texture of Phobos' surface," European Space Agency officials wrote in an MMX mission description.

"The gravity on Phobos is so low that Idefix will only weigh the equivalent of 15 grams [0.5 ounces] on its surface!" they added.

The MMX mothership's Phobos landing will occur in 2030. The spacecraft will grab at least 10 grams (0.4 ounces) of samples from the moon, then head back toward Earth with this extraterrestrial bounty. MMX's return capsule will land here in 2031, after which scientists around the world will scrutinize the Phobos sample for clues about the history and evolution of Mars and our solar system more broadly.

MMX was originally supposed to launch in 2024, but issues with the H3 rocket prevented it from doing so. Mars and Earth align properly for interplanetary launches just once every 26 months, so MMX had to wait a while for its next chance.

Japan already has an impressive sample-return track record. The country's Hayabusa mission brought home pieces of the asteroid Itokawa in 2010, for example, and Hayabusa2 did the same with material from the space rock Ryugu a decade later.

]]> <![CDATA[ Returning the first samples from a Martian moon: Inside the science of Japan's bold MMX mission to Mars ]]> Editor's note: Japan launched its bold MMX sample-return mission to the Mars moon Phobos on Oct. 19) at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT).
Watch a replay of the liftoff and read our launch story here.

Japan's mission to Mars is one of the most ambitious in spaceflight history. It aims to become the first spacecraft to return to Earth from Mars orbit, carrying with it the first-ever samples from the Red Planet system.

The mission, known as Martian Moons eXploration (MMX), is a first-of-its-kind endeavor to study the origin of Mars' moons Phobos and Deimos. The robust undertaking includes a landing on Phobos to collect the samples — which will likely be the first from the Mars system to return to Earth — and a search for evidence that could shed light on events during the formation of the solar system billions of years ago.

MMX launched on an H3 rocket from Japan's Tanegashima Space Center on Monday (Oct. 19) at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. local time in Japan, Oct. 20). After a 10-month journey to reach Mars, the spacecraft will spend about three years studying Phobos, deploying a rover and landing to collect its samples. The mission will then shift its focus to Deimos for a series of flybys before departing for Earth in November 2030. If all goes according to plan, the MMX sample-return capsule is scheduled to land in Australia in 2031.

The spacecraft

The MMX spacecraft is comprised of three main parts, as well as a small rover. After release from its H3 launch vehicle, a propulsion module will provide the boost to put MMX on course for Mars. MMX's main exploration module carries the microwave-size IDEFIX rover and most of the mission's scientific instruments, while the return module houses the sample-return capsule.

Japan's Mitsubishi Electric built MMX's three main modules, with the French space agency CNES (Centre National d'Études Spatiales) and Germany's DLR (Deutsches Zentrum für Luft-und Raumfahrt) jointly developing IDEFIX. The little rover is named for a dog in the 1960s French comic "Asterix," in a nod to the country's first satellite, Astérix, which launched in 1965.

IDEFIX carries a suite of cameras, as well as the Raman Spectrometer for MMX (RAX) and miniaturized radiometer (miniRAD) instruments to analyze Phobos' surface composition and temperature.

Most of MMX's scientific instruments are housed on the exploration module, like NASA's Mars-moon Exploration with Gamma rays and Neutrons (MEGANE, pronounced "meh-gah-nay") device, a gamma-ray and neutron spectrometer built by the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL), and France's MIRS (MMX InfraRed Spectrometer) instrument.

The exploration module also houses the Japanese-built TENGOO (TElescopic Nadir imager for GeOmOrphology) tight-zoom camera, wide-angle OROCHI (Optical RadiOmeter composed of CHromatic Imagers) multispectral camera, laser altimeter (LIDAR) and Mass Spectrum Analyzer (MSA). The return module, meanwhile, carries Japan's Circum-Martian Dust Monitor (CMDM) and Interplanetary Radiation Environment Monitor (IREM).

The mission

MMX will arrive in orbit around Mars in August 2027, at which point it will shed its propulsion module and transition into a quasi-satellite orbit (QSO) around Phobos that allows the probe to fly in a sort of formation with the small, asteroid-sized moon as they both circle the Red Planet.

The spacecraft will spend its first few months in the Martian system observing Phobos from different altitudes, using its TENGOO and OROCHI cameras, LIDAR and MSA to map the moon's surface, study its composition and select potential landing sites.

IDEFIX will be released in late 2028 or early 2029, during the first of two MMX landing rehearsals, at about 130 feet (40 meters) above Phobos. Due to the 14-mile-wide (22 kilometers) moon's extremely low gravity, the rover will be able free-fall to the surface damage-free (hopefully), right itself after a few bounces and begin exploring to gather data on the terrain and surface conditions.

MMX sample collection could begin as early as December 2028, the acting director of NASA's Planetary Science Division, Lindsay Hays, said during a mission briefing on Oct. 15. The spacecraft will attempt two collection landings, with its exploration and return modules descending and returning to orbit as one vehicle.

On Phobos' surface, two different sampling mechanisms — the Corer Sampling Mechanism (C-sampler) and Pneumatic Sampling Mechanism (P-sampler) — will extract and collect at least 10 grams (0.35 ounces) of material for stowage inside the spacecraft's return capsule before MMX lifts off again for orbit. After its first touchdown and sample collection, MMX will return to QSO near Phobos before descending to a second landing site for a similar attempt and subsequent return to orbit.

MMX will end its observations of Phobos after about three years focused on the Martian moon, and will transition into a higher, resonant orbit around Mars in 2030. That course will repeatedly intersect Deimos' path for a series of flybys to collect and compare data with those from Phobos observations as scientists aim to investigate the moons' origins.

Near the end of 2030, the exploration module will separate, leaving the return module to fire its engine out of Mars' gravitational influence and begin an eight-month journey back to Earth with the collected samples. As MMX closes the last stretch of void during its approach to Earth in 2031, the sample-return capsule will separate and enter the atmosphere for a targeted parachute landing in Australia's Woomera region, where its contents will be recovered for laboratory analysis by Japan and its mission partners.

Phobos and Deimos

Those samples, and the data collected by MMX, could tell scientists a lot — about the moons' composition, geography and, perhaps most importantly, how they came to exist in the first place. There are two leading theories for Phobos and Deimos' origins, both of which point to very different versions of ancient Martian history.

"Phobos and Deimos are interesting, but not just in their own right. Their presence is a key piece of the larger story of the Mars system," said Tom Statler, MMX program executive and scientist in NASA's Planetary Science Division, during the Oct. 15 mission briefing. "By uncovering the moons' origin, we'll gain new insights into the history of both Mars and Earth, especially those events that shaped both planets billions of years ago and helped create the worlds we see today."

Both Phobos and Deimos are relatively small and irregularly shaped, and bear several resemblances and spectral characteristics to primitive D-type asteroids — ancient bodies thought to preserve material dating back to the solar system's formation about 4.6 billion years ago. Those similarities suggest Phobos and Deimos may have formed elsewhere in the solar system and were later captured by Mars' gravity.

Their near-circular, equatorially-aligned orbits around the Red Planet, however, somewhat complicate that theory. For example, a captured asteroid would be much more likely to have entered an elongated and tilted orbit akin to the direction and velocity of its original approach, scientists say. A competing hypothesis, therefore, offers a much more violent, but somewhat familiar, narrative for the moons' origins.

An enormous collision with ancient Mars could have blasted material into orbit to form a debris disk from which the two moons eventually coalesced. Such a process, which would be similar to the formation of Earth's moon, could explain their circular, equatorial orbits.

The contradicting geological and orbital observations for Phobos and Deimos collected to date have prevented scientists from definitively establishing one hypothesis over the other. MMX aims to provide an answer.

"It's two totally different lines of evidence that point in two different directions. That's what makes it an interesting puzzle," Statler said. Several theories have also been presented for hybrid scenarios combining the two, he added.

"There's all kinds of different ways, all kinds of different combinations of those two basic scenarios," Statler explained. "But that's the puzzle from the start, the two seemingly contradictory lines of evidence that are pointing us to what … the real history was, but we don't know what it is yet."

The science

Each theory for where Mars' moons came from predicts different chemical characteristics for their surfaces. Presumably, captured asteroids would preserve chemical signatures of material originating elsewhere in the solar system, potentially rich in volatile elements like hydrogen. Moons formed through a planetary impact, however, would contain a mixture of Mars and impact material, altered by the intense heat of such a violent collision.

Determining which scenario is more likely could reveal whether Mars experienced a massive moon-forming collision or acquired its moons from elsewhere in the early solar system. Either answer could offer new insights into the planet's evolution and the events that shaped the terrestrial planets like Earth billions of years ago, mission team members say.

"At this point, we know nothing about the composition of Phobos," David Lawrence, MEGANE principal investigator at APL, said during the Oct. 15 briefing. "We have information about mineralogy, but no elemental composition. And so, elements are really a key way to get at some of these foundational questions."

MMX's scientific suite has been carefully calibrated to make those determinations. The cameras and sensors on the MMX exploration module's TENGOO, OROCHI and LIDAR instruments will map Phobos' terrain, geological features and variations in surface materials from orbit, to provide clues about the moon's formation and evolution. Complementing those measurements, MIRS is designed to detect and classify Phobos' surface minerals and search for organic compounds to further differentiate its possible origin as an asteroid or ancient chunk of Mars.

The RAX spectrometer and miniRAD instrument aboard IDEFIX will add localized context to those observations by examining surface mineralogy and their thermal properties up close.

Back in orbit, NASA's MEGANE instrument will measure Phobos' elemental composition through gamma-ray and neutron spectroscopy that can scan tens of centimeters beneath the moon's surface for signs of volatile elements. Higher abundances of hydrogen, chlorine, sodium and potassium, for instance, would favor the asteroid-capture hypothesis, while lower abundances of those compounds could point to the heat and chemical deterioration associated with a planetary impact.

The JAXA-led mission represents interagency partnerships with NASA and the European Space Agency (ESA), which are providing hardware and communications support through the Deep Space and Estrack networks.

Japan's mission to Mars is one of the most ambitious in spaceflight history. It aims to become the first spacecraft to return to Earth from Mars orbit, carrying with it the first-ever samples from the Red Planet system.

The MMX spacecraft is comprised of three main parts, as well as a small rover. After release from its H3 launch vehicle, a propulsion module will provide the boost to put MMX on course for Mars. The little rover is named for a dog in the 1960s French comic "Asterix," in a nod to the country's first satellite, Astérix, which launched in 1965.

IDEFIX carries a suite of cameras, as well as the Raman Spectrometer for MMX (RAX) and miniaturized radiometer (miniRAD) instruments to analyze Phobos' surface composition and temperature.

MMX will arrive in orbit around Mars in August 2027, at which point it will shed its propulsion module and transition into a quasi-satellite orbit (QSO) around Phobos that allows the probe to fly in a sort of formation with the small, asteroid-sized moon as they both circle the Red Planet.

   <description>Obyvatelé Itálie jsou zděšeni. Mnozí přestali kvůli víkendové vlně násilí a rabování vycházet ven. Opevňují se v bytech a čekají, co bude dál. Část země ovládly chaos, strach a panika. Policisté se stali lovnou zvěří násilníků a nestačí obnovit bezpečí v ulicích.   <item>
   <title>Znásilnění a vražda matky otřásly vesnicí na Plzeňsku. Lidé dodnes nezapomněli</title>
   <link>https://plzensky.denik.cz/krimi/pribehy-zla-plzensko-herbrych-vrah-matka-znasilneni-dozivoti-soudce-jan-speta-vzpominky-sousede/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=krimi</link>
   <description>Když se lidé v Sedlci u Starého Plzence na Plzeňsku dozvěděli, jak skončila jejich bezproblémová sousedka, 68letá Žofie Š., běhal jim mráz po zádech. Starou ženu totiž zavraždil a ještě předtím polomrtvou znásilnil její vlastní syn, kterého si k sobě vzala domů poté, co si odpykal trest za vraždu jiné, 83leté stařenky. O doživotním trestu rozhodl plzeňský soudce Jan Špeta, který na případ, jenž je dalším pokračováním Příběhů zla, pro Deník zavzpomínal, stejně jako někteří obyvatelé Starého Plzence.</description>
   <pubDate>Mon, 19 Oct 2026 11:00:00 +0200</pubDate>
   <guid>https://plzensky.denik.cz/krimi/pribehy-zla-plzensko-herbrych-vrah-matka-znasilneni-dozivoti-soudce-jan-speta-vzpominky-sousede/</guid>

    <item>
      <title>„Kousl ruku, která ho krmila.“ Kreml si vychutnává roztržku Trumpa a Zelenského</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/reuters-kremelsti-jestrabi-si-vychutnavaji-roztrzku-mezi-trumpem-a-zelenskym.A261020_060112_zahranicni_tmps#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Kremelští jestřábi si vychutnávají veřejný rozkol mezi americkým prezidentem Donaldem Trumpem a jeho ukrajinským protějškem Volodymyrem Zelenským. Pro ukrajinskou hlavu státu byl uplynulý týden negativní, zatímco pro Rusko se vyvinul příznivě - přesto se v Moskvě šampaňské zatím stále chladí.</description>

      <description>Na východě Španělska, zejména ve Valencii a v Katalánsku, způsobily silné deště záplavy, kvůli nimž od soboty zemřeli čtyři lidé, informovala dnes místní média. <link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/miton-veri-v-ai-agenty-v-e-commerce-miliony-posila-do-sluzby-ktera-jim-umoznuje-hlidat-ceny-napric-trhem/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Dal&#353;í sázku na AI agenty v e-commerce vypsal Miton, který investuje do českého DeepScoutu, startupu, který právě otevírá svou databázi e-commerce dat umělé inteligenci. Ta je může využít k tvorbě vlastních cenových strategií, analýz a automatizací. Technologie DeepScoutu umí z e-shopů vytáhnout ceny, dostupnost i sortiment a poznat, které produkty si navzájem odpovídají. Doteď ji využívali hlavně velcí obchodníci včetně Alzy.</description>

<item>
<title>Český operátor spouští levnější konkurenci Applu či Googlu pro ukládání obrázků a dokumentů v cloudu</title>

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/floridsky-soud-vydal-zatykac-na-raula-castra-kubanska-vlada-obvineni-vuci_2610192204_jos</link>
 <description>Soud na Floridě vydal v pondělí zatykač na někdejšího kubánského vůdce Raúla Castra, a to na základě obvinění týkajícího se podílu na sestřelení dvou letounů kubánským vojenským letadlem v únoru 1996. Floridská prokuratura 95letého Castra obvinila ze spiknutí za účelem spáchání vraždy prvního stupně, píše web stanice NBC 6.</description>

<item>
 <title>Dav v indické Kolkatě zachvátila panika při oslavách Durgápúdžá. V provizorním chrámu zemřelo 19 lidí</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/dav-v-indicke-kolkate-zachvatila-panika-pri-oslavach-durgapudza-v-provizornim_2610192129_vaa</link>
 <description>Východ Indie slaví v těchto dnech nejdůležitější hinduistické svátky celého roku. Oslavy Durgápúdžá v Západním Bengálsku, které jsou zapsané i na seznamu UNESCO, ale poznamenala tragédie. V tlačenici u provizorního chrámu v Kolkatě zemřelo 19 lidí.</description>

</item>
<item>
 <title>Vztahy Kyjeva a Washingtonu jsou snad na nejnižším bodě, Ukrajinu čeká těžká zima, míní Dorazín</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/vztahy-kyjeva-a-washingtonu-jsou-snad-na-nejnizsim-bode-ukrajinu-ceka-tezka-zima_2610192004_jos</link>
 <description>Ukrajinci dál útočí na ruské rafinerie navzdory tomu, že Donald Trump požádal Kyjev, aby tak nečinili. Neútočení má být mezi Ukrajinou a Ruskem vzájemné, i když Trumpova žádost by byla výrazně výhodnější pro Rusko. „Vztahy mezi Ukrajinou a Spojenými státy mají v sobě sinusoidu, zhoršují se, zlepšují, zhoršují... Teď jsme na bodě, který je pro Ukrajinu asi jeden z nejnižších,“ upozorňuje v Interview Plus stálý zpravodaj na Ukrajině Martin Dorazín.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/e00761a7243395c3d5f1f39d6063c1c2.jpg?itok=0jcGgOn2" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Mon, 19 Oct 2026 20:04:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Francouzské úřady vyhlásily kvůli protestům zákaz vycházení. Platí v Paříži i severském Lille</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/francouzske-urady-vyhlasily-kvuli-protestum-zakaz-vychazeni-plati-v-lille-a_2610191840_jos</link>
 <description>Po víkendových nepokojích a násilnostech v řadě francouzských měst vyhlásily úřady zákaz vycházení v Paříži, Lille a jeho okolních městech na severu země, platný od pondělních 20.00 do úterních 6.00. 
Informovaly o tom francouzská televizní stanice BFM a agentura Reuters s odvoláním na zdroj z kanceláře premiéra Sebastiena Lecornua. Zákaz vycházení platí dva dny a týká se také měst Douai, Wattignies a Denain, dodal zdroj.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/img_7539_261018-201806_vdv.jpeg?itok=P9hp0vEs" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Mon, 19 Oct 2026 18:40:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>‚Mimořádně složitá operace.‘ Dron na Ukrajině poprvé evakuoval zraněného vojáka</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/online-mimoradne-slozita-operace-dron-na-ukrajine-poprve-evakuoval-zraneneho_2610191720_jos</link>
 <description>Ukrajinská armáda poprvé z frontové linie evakuovala zraněného vojáka za pomoci bezpilotního letounu. Na telegramu o tom v pondělí informovala samostatná 92. útočná brigáda Ivana Sirka i firma, která stroj vyvinula. Ukrajina se od začátku ruské invaze v únoru 2022 stala průkopníkem ve vývoji a využívání bezpilotních systémů na bojišti.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/3228ff153b1fcdca3b1a2737129a322a.jpg?itok=9hU7hIiG" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Mon, 19 Oct 2026 17:20:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>‚Sdílejte jízdu, nikoliv hluk.‘ Britská vláda zavádí opatření proti hlasité hudbě v hromadné dopravě</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/sdilejte-jizdu-nikoliv-hluk-britska-vlada-zavadi-opatreni-proti-hlasite-hudbe-v_2610191616_jos</link>
 <description>Cestování hromadnou dopravou v Anglii by mohlo být příjemnější. Vláda spouští kampaň namířenou proti asociálnímu chování. Cílí na odhazování odpadků, používání elektronických cigaret, výhružné chování a také hluk. Za porušení pravidel hrozí nově pokuta ve výši sto liber, tedy asi 2800 korun.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/ant-rozetsky-lr9vo8m_200821-154350_rez.jpg?itok=ZGhISPK4" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Mon, 19 Oct 2026 16:16:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Někde to vypadá, že se nic neděje. Kousek dál se ale rabují obchody, popisuje Češka situaci v Paříži</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/nekde-vypada-ze-se-nic-nedeje-kousek-dal-se-ale-rabuji-obchody-popisuje-ceska_2610191334_adn</link>
 <description>Požár radnice v Limoges, stovky vyrabovaných obchodů, útoky na sídla úřadů, násilí v ulicích a ostré střety s policií. Tak také vypadal víkend ve Francii, kde do ulic vyšly statisíce lidí na protest proti zdražování energií a dalších životních nákladů. „Škody jsou veliké, spousta spálených aut, spousta vyrabovaných obchodů,“ popisuje pro Radiožurnál Pavlína Koubská, státní úřednice v Paříži.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-17t154742z_1_261017-175431_nel.JPG?itok=PC16ZAvA" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Mon, 19 Oct 2026 13:34:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Po útocích na americkou novinářku a evropské diplomaty zadržela izraelská policie osm podezřelých</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/po-utocich-na-americkou-novinarku-a-evropske-diplomaty-zadrzela-izraelska_2610191132_adn</link>
 <description>Izraelská policie zadržela osm podezřelých v rámci vyšetřování víkendových násilností na okupovaném Západním břehu, mezi nimiž byly i útoky na americkou fotoreportérku a evropské diplomaty. Informovala o tom v pondělí agentura Reuters, která podotýká, že stíhání izraelských osadníků je vzácné.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-13t111614z_1_261019-112433_adn.JPG?itok=k8gk81jL" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
<item>
 <title>‚Nevím, kde to Zelenskyj bere.‘ Rubio popřel, že USA stoply sdílení zpravodajských informací</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/online-nevim-kde-zelenskyj-bere-rubio-poprel-ze-usa-stoply-sdileni_2610191113_mst</link>
 <description>Americký ministr zahraničí Marco Rubio v pondělí popřel, že Spojené státy pozastavily sdílení některých zpravodajských informací s Ukrajinou. Píše o tom agentura Reuters, podle které je vyjádření šéfa americké diplomacie v rozporu s výroky ukrajinského prezidenta Volodymyra Zelenského. Ten v pondělí znovu řekl, že Ukrajina nedostala od partnerů varování před nočním ruským raketovým útokem.</description>

<description>Dal&#353;í sázku na AI agenty v e-commerce vypsal Miton, který investuje do českého DeepScoutu, startupu, který právě otevírá svou databázi e-commerce dat umělé inteligenci.
